content: Indinavir is metabolized by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. When co-administered with indinavir, the following interactions occur: 1. Velpatasvir: Indinavir (5 mg/24 hr) increases the level or effect of velpatasvir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 2. Vemurafenib: Vemurafenib increases indinavir levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Venlafaxine: Indinavir increases the level or effect of venlafaxine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Verapamil: Indinavir increases the level or effect of verapamil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, verapamil increases indinavir levels via both CYP3A4 inhibition and P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Vilanterol/Fluticasone Furoate (Inhaled): Indinavir increases the level or effect of these agents by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both are CYP3A4 substrates, and co-administration with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 6. Vincristine Liposomal: Indinavir increases the level or effect of vincristine liposomal by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Vortioxetine: Indinavir increases the level or effect of vortioxetine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Warfarin: Indinavir increases the level or effect of warfarin through mechanisms involving CYP3A4, CYP1A2, and CYP2C19 metabolism. Monitor INR more frequently and adjust the warfarin dose as needed. 9. Zanubrutinib: Indinavir increases the level or effect of zanubrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce zanubrutinib to 80 mg once daily if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Interrupt dosing for adverse reactions and resume the previous dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor. 10. Zidovudine: Indinavir and zidovudine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Zileuton: Indinavir increases the level or effect of zileuton by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Zuranolone: Indinavir increases the level or effect of zuranolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the zuranolone dose if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 13. Acetazolamide: Acetazolamide increases the level or effect of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 14. Alfentanil: Indinavir increases the level or effect of alfentanil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 15. Aliskiren: Indinavir increases the level or effect of aliskiren by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 16. Alosetron: Indinavir increases the level or effect of alosetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 17. Alvimopan: Indinavir increases the level or effect of alvimopan by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. The clinical significance is unknown. 18. Ambrisentan: Indinavir increases the level or effect of ambrisentan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 19. Anastrozole: Anastrozole increases the level or effect of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 20. Armodafinil: Indinavir increases the level or effect of armodafinil by inhibiting both CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. The clinical significance is unknown. 21. Atazanavir: Indinavir increases the level or effect of atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 22. Bosentan: Indinavir increases the level or effect of bosentan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 23. Cevimeline: Indinavir increases the level or effect of cevimeline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 24. Clarithromycin: Indinavir increases the level or effect of clarithromycin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 25. Cyclophosphamide: Cyclophosphamide increases the level or effect of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 26. Danazol: Danazol increases the level or effect of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 27. Dapsone: Indinavir increases the level or effect of dapsone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 28. Disopyramide: Indinavir increases the level or effect of disopyramide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 29. Docetaxel: Indinavir increases the level or effect of docetaxel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 30. Donepezil: Indinavir increases the level or effect of donepezil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 31. Drospirenone: Drospirenone increases the level or effect of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 32. Dutasteride: Indinavir increases the level or effect of dutasteride by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 33. Efavirenz: Indinavir increases the level or effect of efavirenz by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 34. Eplerenone: Indinavir increases the level or effect of eplerenone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 35. Eucalyptus: Indinavir increases the level or effect of eucalyptus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 36. Fexofenadine: Indinavir increases the level or effect of fexofenadine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. The clinical significance is unknown. 37. Finasteride: Indinavir increases the level or effect of finasteride by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 38. Food: Food decreases indinavir levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral form of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 39. Ganaxolone: Indinavir affects ganaxolone exposure via CYP3A4 metabolism. Changes in ganaxolone exposure with CYP3A4 inhibitors are not expected to be clinically significant. 40. Imatinib: Indinavir increases the level or effect of imatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 41. Isradipine: Indinavir increases the level or effect of isradipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 42. Ixazomib: Indinavir affects ixazomib exposure via CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical trials show no meaningful change in systemic exposure when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 43. Ketoconazole: Indinavir increases the level or effect of ketoconazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 44. Lansoprazole: Indinavir increases the level or effect of lansoprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 45. Levoketoconazole: Indinavir increases the level or effect of levoketoconazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 46. Loratadine: Indinavir increases the level or effect of loratadine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. The clinical significance is unknown. 47. Montelukast: Indinavir increases the level or effect of montelukast by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 48. Nimodipine: Indinavir increases the level or effect of nimodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 49. Nitrendipine: Indinavir increases the level or effect of nitrendipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 50. Oxybutynin: Indinavir increases the level or effect of oxybutynin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 51. Paclitaxel Protein-Bound: Indinavir increases the level or effect of paclitaxel protein-bound by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 53. Parecoxib: Indinavir increases the level or effect of parecoxib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 54. Pioglitazone: Indinavir increases the level or effect of pioglitazone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 55. Propafenone: Indinavir increases the level or effect of propafenone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 56. Quinine: Indinavir increases the level or effect of quinine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 57. Quizartinib: Indinavir increases the level or effect of quizartinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce quizartinib dose to 4 mg/day when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor. 58. Rabeprazole: Indinavir increases the level or effect of rabeprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 59. Ramelteon: Indinavir increases the level or effect of ramelteon by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 60. Sufentanil: Indinavir increases the level or effect of sufentanil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 61. Vinblastine: Indinavir increases the level or effect of vinblastine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 62. Vincristine: Indinavir increases the level or effect of vincristine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 63. Vincristine Liposomal: Indinavir increases the level or effect of vincristine liposomal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 64. Vinorelbine: Indinavir increases the level or effect of vinorelbine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 65. Zaleplon: Indinavir increases the level or effect of zaleplon by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 66. Ziprasidone: Indinavir increases the level or effect of ziprasidone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 67. Zolpidem: Indinavir increases the level or effect of zolpidem by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 68. Zonisamide: Indinavir increases the level or effect of zonisamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 69. Abacavir: Indinavir and abacavir both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 70. Abemaciclib: Indinavir increases the level or effect of abemaciclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase plasma levels of abemaciclib and its metabolites, requiring dose reduction. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor. 71. Acalabrutinib: Indinavir increases the level or effect of acalabrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If short-term use of the inhibitor is necessary, temporarily interrupt acalabrutinib treatment. 72. Acarbose: Indinavir decreases the effects of acarbose through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Hyperglycemia and new-onset diabetes mellitus have been reported with protease inhibitors. 73. Adagrasib: Indinavir increases the level or effect of adagrasib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors until adagrasib reaches steady-state (~8 days).
